content.title: About
content.content: Potato, roasted, ready-to-heat are pre‑cooked potato slices or cubes that have been fried to a golden crisp and packaged in single‑serve portions. They only need to be reheated in a microwave or oven and are ready to serve as a side dish or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: When quickly frozen after frying, roasted potatoes retain a high amount of vitamin C.
A double‑fry method (first at medium heat, then high) is often used to achieve extra crunch.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed foods; ready‑to‑heat roasted versions are popular in fast‑paced societies.
With proper packaging, the product can keep its taste and texture for up to 12 months.
Flavor varieties include herb‑seasoned, cheese‑coated, spicy, and even sweet cinnamon‑infused versions.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide steady energy through slowly digestible starches, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports immune function and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids fluid balance and promotes healthy heart function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low sodium when unsalted
items.content: Unsalted versions can be a good choice for low‑sodium diets.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Because the potatoes are fried, they contain added oils, making them more calorie‑dense than boiled potatoes.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Some products are heavily salted or contain preservatives; people with hypertension should opt for low‑salt varieties.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature frying can create acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound; manufacturers aim to keep its levels low.

items.title: Allergy to seasonings
items.content: The product may include flavorings or spices that can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the package in the microwave (2‑3 minutes) or in an oven at 180 °C (350 °F) for 10‑12 minutes. Serve as a side with meat, fish, or enjoy as a snack, topped with fresh herbs, cheese, or your favorite dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the remaining portion refrigerated and consume within 3‑5 days.
